original_value: We study a locally differentially private frequency estimation problem in which a server must recover the most frequent items from a large domain while preserving user privacy. We propose a new randomized sketching algorithm that achieves near-optimal error as a function of the domain size, the privacy budget, and the failure probability. Our approach combines compressed representations of user reports with a refined decoding procedure that improves upon standard count-sketch style baselines. We also establish lower bounds showing that the dependence on the failure probability is unavoidable in the local model. In addition, we derive a transformation that converts a broad class of interactive local protocols into simpler non-interactive mechanisms with only a modest loss in accuracy. These results have applications to histogram release, frequency moments, and robust data analytics under privacy constraints.

result.paraphrase: We investigate frequency estimation under local differential privacy, where a server must identify the most common items in a large domain while protecting user privacy. We introduce a new randomized sketching method that attains near-optimal error in terms of the domain size, privacy budget, and failure probability. The method uses compressed user reports together with an improved decoding algorithm that outperforms standard count-sketch-style baselines. We also prove lower bounds demonstrating that dependence on the failure probability cannot be avoided in the local model. Additionally, we present a transformation that turns a wide class of interactive local protocols into simpler non-interactive mechanisms with only a modest loss of accuracy. These findings apply to histogram release, frequency moments, and privacy-preserving robust data analytics.
